questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes colonization from infection?
choices: Colonization always requires antibiotics
Colonization is organism presence without disease caused by tissue invasion
Infection is defined by a positive culture alone
Colonization only occurs in hospitalized patients
questions.explanation: Colonization means organisms may be present without a compatible illness caused by those organisms. Clinical syndrome and context determine whether treatment is appropriate.

questions.question: What is the best first question before choosing an outpatient antibiotic?
choices: Which broad-spectrum agent is easiest to prescribe?
Does this patient have a bacterial infection likely to benefit from antimicrobial therapy?
Which antibiotic has the longest duration?
Which medication is newest?
questions.explanation: A defensible diagnosis comes before antimicrobial selection. Antibiotics do not treat viral or noninfectious conditions.

questions.question: What does empiric antimicrobial therapy mean?
choices: Treatment selected after susceptibility results are known
Initial treatment selected using likely pathogens, syndrome severity, and patient factors
Using two antibiotics for every infection
Continuing the same drug regardless of results
questions.explanation: Empiric therapy is the reasoned initial treatment before complete microbiology information is available.

questions.question: What is de-escalation after culture results return?
choices: Increasing spectrum automatically
Narrowing, simplifying, changing, or stopping therapy when clinical context supports it
Ignoring culture results if the patient feels better
Changing treatment only after a severe adverse event
questions.explanation: De-escalation is active, evidence-based reassessment that can reduce unnecessary exposure and collateral harm.

questions.question: Which factor is most important when interpreting a positive culture?
choices: The test result alone
Symptoms, examination, specimen quality, site, host risk, and the result
Whether the patient wants an antibiotic
Whether the result is printed in red
questions.explanation: A positive culture can represent contamination or colonization. It must be interpreted with the clinical syndrome and specimen context.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate reason to reassess antimicrobial selection during acute kidney injury?
choices: Every antibiotic is safe at any dose in AKI
Some drugs or metabolites may accumulate and increase toxicity risk
Kidney function affects only viral medications
A serum creatinine makes clinical assessment unnecessary
questions.explanation: Kidney function can alter clearance and toxicity risk. Use current drug-specific dosing guidance and reassess the whole patient.

questions.question: A patient reports a “penicillin allergy.” What is the most useful next step?
choices: Assume every related medication is permanently contraindicated
Ask which drug caused what reaction, timing, severity, and later tolerance
Prescribe an antibiotic without discussing it
Tell the patient the label never matters
questions.explanation: A detailed reaction history helps distinguish non-allergic effects, lower-risk histories, immediate hypersensitivity, and severe delayed reactions.

questions.question: Which presentation most strongly suggests that routine outpatient oral treatment may be unsafe?
choices: Mild symptoms with normal vital signs and reliable follow-up
Urinary symptoms with fever, vomiting, flank pain, tachycardia, and poor oral intake
A request for symptom counseling
A patient asking about medication cost
questions.explanation: Systemic toxicity, flank pain, vomiting, and poor intake raise concern for a complicated or upper-tract infection and may require urgent higher-level evaluation.

questions.question: Why is source control important in antimicrobial management?
choices: Antibiotics always replace drainage or procedures
Some infections require drainage, device assessment, or relief of obstruction in addition to medication
Source control only applies to viral illness
It eliminates the need for follow-up
questions.explanation: Medication alone may be insufficient when an abscess, obstruction, infected device, or deep infection requires procedural management.

questions.question: Which plan best reflects outpatient antimicrobial stewardship?
choices: Use the broadest agent for the longest duration whenever symptoms are present
Prescribe only when indicated; use current guidance, counsel the patient, and set follow-up and red flags
Avoid cultures in all patients
Continue a drug even when results and diagnosis do not support infection
questions.explanation: Stewardship aims for the right drug, dose, route, and duration only when needed, with education and reassessment.
